decisions.reason: The existing message-61 MODIFY already requires the solenoid dispensing mechanism to be integrated into the layout and CAD; the wiring-plan change entails no additional candidate-state update.
The existing message-61 MODIFY already records the solenoid valve as a required dispensing component; adding its control wiring to the wiring plan does not further change the BOM requirement.
The existing message-61 MODIFY already captures the solenoid-valve control mechanism and dispensing sequence; documenting its wiring does not change the dispensing behavior.
Including solenoid control wiring in the wiring plan does not necessarily change the existing strategy of using off-the-shelf electronic components.
The wiring-plan change does not alter the plumbing seal requirements, which are already independently reaffirmed by message 61.
Electrical control wiring for the solenoid does not change the existing requirement that seals prevent liquid from reaching electrical components.
The wiring-plan addition does not change the spout's geometry, material, mounting location, or orientation.
Adding solenoid control wiring to the wiring plan does not alter the requirement for removable or easily cleaned dispensing parts.
The solenoid wiring-plan change has no necessary effect on structural stability or vibration-control requirements.
The source does not change the prototype's selected 120V wall-power source or its scope.
The existing message-61 MODIFY independently captures the splash target and optional guard; solenoid control wiring adds no further splash-control state.
The solenoid wiring-plan change does not resolve the whisk-head ambiguity or otherwise change mixing and frothing performance requirements.
